title: Ehelepola Walauwa Wax Museum — character roster and curatorial presentation
date: museum opened 2025; site and supplied sitemap accessed 2026-08-26
author_or_institution: Ehelepola Walauwa Wax Museum / Sri Dalada Maligawa
scope: Present-day museum roster and curatorial framing of Kandyan kings, nobles, religious figures, colonial intermediaries and the Ehelepola family
limitations: Ranked at the same navigation level as Wikipedia by user instruction. The JavaScript site did not expose stable individual texts to direct retrieval; it is evidence for current museum framing and a lead for research, not independent proof of historical events or motives.

title: Between the Portuguese and the Nayakas: the many faces of the Kandyan Kingdom, 1591–1765
scope: Cosmopolitan court culture, Portuguese and Nayaka connections, conversion, exile, dynastic adaptation and Kandyan kingship from 1591 to 1765
limitations: Synthetic scholarly chapter; individual biographical episodes remain dependent on uneven Portuguese, Dutch and chronicle traditions and should not be romanticized.

title: Thailand's Sublime Gift to Sri Lanka
author_or_institution: Lorna Dewaraja / Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of Sri Lanka
scope: 1753 Ayutthaya mission, Upali Thera, Kirti Sri Rajasinghe, higher ordination and establishment of the Siam Nikaya
limitations: Strong for the institutional mission and religious network; it does not by itself establish the social reach, later caste restrictions or uniformity of the revived order.

title: Sir John D'Oyly, the Strategist
date: 1815 archival record; National Archives exhibit accessed 2026-08-26
author_or_institution: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka
scope: D'Oyly's Sinhala studies, cultural contacts, intelligence role, efforts to create discord among Kandyan nobles and drafting of the 1815 Convention; includes archival reference LK-NA/21/35/1
limitations: Institutional synthesis built around a cited colonial letter. It demonstrates British strategy and official appraisal, not that every noble acted from the same motive or that intelligence alone caused the takeover.

title: Cosmopolitanism and indigeneity in four violent years: the fall of the kingdom of Kandy and the Great Rebellion revisited
scope: Political and social reconfiguration surrounding the 1815 fall and 1817–18 rebellion, including the instability of simple indigenous/foreign binaries
limitations: Macro-historical interpretation; use with the National Archives record for D'Oyly's specific operational role.
